facts.blocked_reason: No failure drill has been executed against this candidate or this infrastructure. Two of the three prerequisites the previous pass recorded are now cleared, and clearing them exposed a third that no credential or permission can address. CLEARED: the two mandatory 24 kHz mono s16 PCM prompts now have a documented ten-second regeneration procedure and a pinned machine-local location (openagents dd5d62a5dd), proven by a live two-journey acceptance run that passed with Sarah audio, ephemeral transcription, and exact settlement in both journeys. CLEARED: the automation identity now holds a namespace-scoped RBAC Role in livekit-system granting exactly pods:delete and pods/log:get,list, verified by real API calls rather than kubectl auth can-i, which answers optimistically for subresources and returned a false yes for pods/log. STILL BLOCKED, and this is the binding constraint: there is no single-session driver. runSarahLiveKitAcceptance requires both a private and a community scenario, runs them concurrently, hard-asserts concurrent overlap, and returns only after both settle, so nothing can hold one session live while a fault is injected into it. That blocks worker_crash, sfu_loss, provider_disconnect, timeout, hold_exhaustion, and reconnect alike. sfu_loss additionally requires concurrentBillableSessionCount: 1, which that driver can never produce; its step 2 is also unsolved under the granted authority, because it reads livekit_room_total through pods/exec, which was deliberately not granted, and the Managed Prometheus substitute scrapes every 30 s against a session that lives about 21 s. membership_revocation_bounded and hold_exhaustion_bounded have no operator path at all: the only revocation lever revokes every active alpha member with no bulk re-admit, and no checked-in tool derives the worker control bearer. replayed_grant_refused has no defined procedure. duplicate_participant_refused still has no production code path. The provider-disconnect route remains contract-locked closed; arming was authorized for this lane but not performed, because the drill it enables still needs the missing driver, and an armed window that cannot be used is production mutation without evidence. The eight-scope privacy scan is no longer blocked: a separate lane cleared all four blockers and defined the three prose-only scopes (openagents c1a54c919d), and this lane injected the retention canaries that scan needs, because a canary generated at scan time tests nothing. The canaries were spoken into real production sessions in the window 2026-07-31T18:41:26Z to 18:41:51Z with transcription observed on both journeys. The scan itself has still produced no receipt, so privacy_scope_count remains not_observed. No media-key rekey proof exists.

facts.note: This receipt records what was actually observed for one Sarah LiveKit release-gate row on Omega v0.2.0-rc29. It never promotes source tests, configuration, deployment-lifecycle receipts, or a headless harness run into an installed packaged-candidate observation.
refused_claims: Arming, or being able to arm, the provider-disconnect route is not evidence that the drill passed; the flag is false, so it was never even armed.
A checked-in static E2EE key revision value is configuration, not a rekey proof.
Unit tests of the failure-matrix contract and of replay, duplicate-claim, and revocation refusals are source evidence and do not stand in for executed drills.

Clearing the PCM and cluster-authority blockers is not progress toward green for this row. No drill ran, and the driver gap that remains blocks strictly more scenarios than either cleared blocker did.
A passing live acceptance run is not a failure drill. It proves the prompts and the session path work; it injects no fault and settles no scenario under one.

kubectl auth can-i is not evidence of a cluster permission. It answered yes for pods/log while the real call was Forbidden, and the shared gke-gcloud-auth-plugin token cache outside CLOUDSDK_CONFIG can silently answer as a different identity.
The first gate observation receipt is not a gate result. Every one of its ten observations is not_observed and its outcome is incomplete.
Injecting retention canaries is not a privacy scan result. It removes a false-clean risk on one axis of a scan that has still not been run.

A clean retention result would be bounded by the retention horizon of whatever the canaries entered. A scan run long after the injection window may find nothing because the material aged out, not because nothing retained it.

facts.unblocks_when: A single-session drill driver exists that admits one scenario, completes a turn, and holds the session open until the operator injects a fault and releases it. That is now the binding prerequisite: it blocks six of the ten observations by itself, and it is a repository change, unlike the two prerequisites cleared on 2026-07-31. With it, the eight bounded drills are executed against this infrastructure binding with deterministic settlement preserved for each, the eight-scope privacy scan produces a same-window complete export, and a media-key rekey is observed. Any scenario that cannot be executed is recorded inconclusive rather than passed. Four gaps additionally need a decision rather than a run: sfu_loss step 2 needs either pods/exec or a faster scrape, membership_revocation and hold_exhaustion need bounded operator paths that do not exist, and replayed_grant_refused needs a defined procedure.
